title: When Models Build Their Own Machines: From Silicon to Self-Scaling Intelligence
content: Every model runs on a machine it did not design. This is changing. Language models write RTL, tune kernels and orchestrate EDA flows. They are beginning to help design the chips that train and serve them. As models improve chips and chips train stronger models, intelligence may scale beyond software alone. We treat the chip as the physical layer of recursive self-improvement, describe the co-evolution of model, software stack and silicon as a dynamical system, and propose the Levels of Self-Scaling Intelligence L0–L6, from design assistance, autonomous optimization and end-to-end design to self-improvement and cross-layer co-evolution, with recursive self-expansion and open-ended autonomous evolution as the horizon. Across over 400 works, we find that in three years language models have covered most of the ground within a single layer, yet decisions that cross layer boundaries are still mostly made by people, and very few works close the loop between silicon and intelligence. The loop breaks in three places: silicon feedback is slow and sparse, agents' horizons and training environments are confined to a single layer, and the ecosystem is fragmented. Intelligence was once shaped by machines; now it is beginning to shape them. The loop is not yet finished, and its next line may well be written by the machines themselves.
